newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power holds in light trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power holds in light trading.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. were mostly steady Tuesday in very light trading due to reduced generation capacity and weak power demand, industry sources said.
"The load has been way down. I don't expect any changes throughout the week. Everyone is running oil units," said one power marketer.
Although temperatures are near-normal in the Northeast now, temperatures are expected to slip as the week progresses.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), next-day non-firm power prices during peak hours were discussed in the $28.50-29.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared to the $28.50 quotes seen on Monday.
Off-peak, non-firm power prices in NEPOOL for Wednesday were again seen around $19.50.
For January/February 1997 NEPOOL deliveries, non-firm prices were discussed in the $35.00 area.
In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), peak, non-firm prices in the western portion of the system were still talked in the $18.75 area, with very little business reported done.
November non-firm prices were in the $23.50-24.00 area, while December business was reported done in the $25.00-26.00 range.
